measurements.note:
[engine] Only prism has the clock keeper and the line that fixes the draft's ubatch (fork mango-prism, common/speculative.cpp).
[env] Clock keeper: see bonsai2, +27-39% decode on the 3.6. LLAMA_MTP_UBATCH: the draft's context copied the model's ubatch and reserved a full-model compute buffer (432 MiB at 128k); at 32 it is 294, and that is what makes the draft fit at 128k.
[spec] MTP draft, lossless. MEASURED 2026-10-26 from the server (summary and code, temperature 0, 256 tokens), same config without draft -> with draft: idle decode 50 -> 59-60, at 64k 28-29 -> 35/43, at 118k 21 -> 31/29. Drafts accepted 65-83%. n-max 3 wins on code (+8-10%) and loses on prose (-4-12%): 2 is the most balanced. It costs prefill: 716 -> 466 tok/s at 64k (the head rereads the prompt, and -ts 16,16,10 puts one layer on the 1080, which is slow at prefill).
[kv] Model q8_0, draft f16. With more tokens at a time (prompt prefill, draft verification) flash attention converts the whole KV of a layer to f16, and the compute buffer reserves that copy: 256 MiB per GPU at 128k. For the model (3-4 attention layers per GPU) q8_0 is still better than f16; for the draft (one layer) f16 costs less: 272 MiB against 136+256.
[fit] --fit is on by default on prism and would move weights to RAM without saying so: here an OOM must stay an OOM.
[why] MoE: 35B of weights at rest but only 3B active per token. MEASURED 2026-10-26 at 128k: VRAM 7543/7519/5373 MiB, the margin is small (at 128k the three GPUs have ~1 GB of real memory left, not the 3 that CUDA reports as free). Before (mango engine, no draft): 50.6/39.2 idle, 26.4/22.9 at 64k, 16.7/14.4 at 118k. --no-mmproj-offload keeps the vision encoder in RAM. 256k goes OOM.
[ub] No -ub: with the default 512 pipeline parallelism does not fit and llama.cpp falls back to running without it by itself (it is like this without the draft too). -ub 256 would make it fit and leave the draft without space; measured, the pipeline does not help prefill on these GPUs.
[ts] In LAYERS (42 = 40 + MTP + output). The automatic split (16/15/11) puts the last layer, the output and the whole draft on the 1660S: OOM. One layer moves to the 1080, which at 128k had 774 MiB free.
